front.title: Post-Quantum Traditional (PQ/T) Hybrid PKI Authentication with separate certificates in the Internet Key Exchange Version 2 (IKEv2)

abstract.t: A Cryptographically Relevant Quantum Computer (CRQC) would break the traditional asymmetric algorithms, such as RSA and ECDSA, that are widely used to authenticate the Internet Key Exchange Protocol Version 2 (IKEv2). Post-quantum digital signature algorithms are intended to resist such a computer, but these new algorithms and their implementations require time to mature. This document specifies a post-quantum traditional (PQ/T) hybrid PKI authentication method for IKEv2 in which each peer uses two separate certificates: one containing a post-quantum public key and one containing a traditional public key. Authentication remains secure as long as at least one of the component signature algorithms remains secure.
